correctness.rationale: Bu et al. Theorem 5.1 gives common-two-value existence with ex-post EFX+fPO. For the stated three-level 3×4 matrix, any EFX allocation has nonempty bundles and pattern (2,1,1); evaluating 36 pair/singleton configurations yields exactly 14 EFX, of which exactly five survive integral PO against all 81 complete allocations. Their ex-ante envy inequalities have surpluses (0,0,3,−1,−1), (1,1,−2,−1,−1), (−3,−3,5,3,3). The combination 3d13+d32=−y forces y=0; d12=−z then z=0; d32=−3x forces x=0, contradicting x+y+z=1. Independent enumeration reconstructed the 81/14/5 counts and exact certificate.

value.rationale: Determining the sharp shared singleton-value alphabet boundary between universal best-of-both-worlds existence and failure is a natural parameter question. The new exact three-level witness and compact impossibility certificate sharpen a previously known unrestricted impossibility theorem, without claiming the general no-lottery phenomenon as new.
